Author: Prashant Khoje <prashant.khoje@neurealm.com>
Date:   Thu Jan 29 22:15:28 2026 +0530

    ppc64le - Fix deviation in floating point values caused by FMA (#91)
    
    This was exposed while testing CockroachDB.
    Following tests from pkg/sql/opt/exec/execbuilder fail due to floating point precision differences caused by FMA:
    - TestExecBuild/local/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/local-vec-off/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/local-spec-planning/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/fakedist/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/fakedist-vec-off/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/fakedist-metadata/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/fakedist-disk/geospatial
    - TestExecBuild/fakedist-spec-planning/geospatial
    
    With explicit casts in this patch, these failures are resolved.
    
    References:
    https://go.dev/ref/spec#Floating_point_operators
    https://github.com/golang/go/issues/53297
    https://github.com/golang/go/issues/48145
    https://github.com/disintegration/gift/issues/20#issuecomment-524551797
    
    Co-authored-by: Prashant Khoje <prashant.khoje@ibm.com>
    Co-authored-by: Prashant Khoje <prashant.khoje@gslab.com>

Author: Robert Snedegar <viking@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri May 31 06:24:00 2019 +1000

    s2: Add type tags to the Shape interface.
    
    This begins the support for different encoding mechanisms and options,
    mirroring C++.
    
    Signed-off-by: David Symonds <dsymonds@golang.org>

diff --git a/s2/polygon.go b/s2/polygon.go
index 3b25df8..57c43fb 100644
--- a/s2/polygon.go
+++ b/s2/polygon.go
@@ -814,6 +814,8 @@ func (p *Polygon) ChainPosition(edgeID int) ChainPosition {
 // Dimension returns the dimension of the geometry represented by this Polygon.
 func (p *Polygon) Dimension() int { return 2 }
 
+func (p *Polygon) typeTag() typeTag { return typeTagPolygon }
+
 func (p *Polygon) privateInterface() {}
 
 // Contains reports whether this polygon contains the other polygon.
diff --git a/s2/shape.go b/s2/shape.go
index 4731fa4..2cbf170 100644
--- a/s2/shape.go
+++ b/s2/shape.go
@@ -114,6 +114,23 @@ func OriginReferencePoint(contained bool) ReferencePoint {
 	return ReferencePoint{Point: OriginPoint(), Contained: contained}
 }
 
+// typeTag is a 32-bit tag that can be used to identify the type of an encoded
+// Shape. All encodable types have a non-zero type tag. The tag associated with
+type typeTag uint32
+
+const (
+	// Indicates that a given Shape type cannot be encoded.
+	typeTagNone        typeTag = 0
+	typeTagPolygon     typeTag = 1
+	typeTagPolyline    typeTag = 2
+	typeTagPointVector typeTag = 3
+	typeTagLaxPolyline typeTag = 4
+	typeTagLaxPolygon  typeTag = 5
+
+	// The minimum allowable tag for future user-defined Shape types.
+	typeTagMinUser typeTag = 8192
+)
+
 // Shape represents polygonal geometry in a flexible way. It is organized as a
 // collection of edges that optionally defines an interior. All geometry
 // represented by a given Shape must have the same dimension, which means that
@@ -220,6 +237,10 @@ type Shape interface {
 	// IsFull reports whether the Shape contains all points on the sphere.
 	IsFull() bool
 
+	// typeTag returns a value that can be used to identify the type of an
+	// encoded Shape.
+	typeTag() typeTag
+
 	// We do not support implementations of this interface outside this package.
 	privateInterface()
 }

+func (s *ShapeIndex) encode(e *encoder) {
+	e.writeInt8(shapeIndexEncodingVersion)
+	e.writeInt32(int32(s.maxEdgesPerCell))
+	e.writeInt32(s.nextID)
+	e.writeInt32(s.pendingAdditionsPos)
+
+	// Shapes:
+	e.writeUint32(uint32(len(s.shapes)))
+	// Write shapes in sorted order by shapeID for determinism
+	shapeIDs := make([]int32, 0, len(s.shapes))
+	for id := range s.shapes {
+		shapeIDs = append(shapeIDs, id)
+	}
+	slices.Sort(shapeIDs)
+
+	for _, id := range shapeIDs {
+		shape := s.shapes[id]
+		if shape == nil {
+			e.err = fmt.Errorf("cannot encode nil shape with ID %d", id)
+			return
+		}
+		tag := shape.typeTag()
+		if tag == typeTagNone {
+			e.err = fmt.Errorf("cannot encode shape %d: unsupported shape type %T", id, shape)
+			return
+		}
+		e.writeInt32(id)
+		e.writeUint32(uint32(tag))
+		encodeShape(e, shape)
+		if e.err != nil {
+			return
+		}
+	}
+
+	// Cells:
+	e.writeUint32(uint32(len(s.cells)))
+	for _, cellID := range s.cells {
+		cell := s.cellMap[cellID]
+		e.writeUint64(uint64(cellID))
+		if cell == nil {
+			e.writeUint32(0)
+			continue
+		}
+		e.writeUint32(uint32(len(cell.shapes)))
+		for _, cs := range cell.shapes {
+			e.writeInt32(cs.shapeID)
+			e.writeBool(cs.containsCenter)
+			e.writeUint32(uint32(len(cs.edges)))
+			for _, edgeID := range cs.edges {
+				e.writeInt32(int32(edgeID))
+			}
+		}
+		if e.err != nil {
+			return
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func encodeShape(e *encoder, shape Shape) {
+	switch s := shape.(type) {
+	case *Polygon:
+		s.encode(e)
+	case *Polyline:
+		s.encode(e)
+	case *PointVector:
+		s.encode(e)
+	case *LaxPolyline:
+		s.encode(e)
+	case *LaxPolygon:
+		s.encode(e)
+	case *Loop:
+		s.encode(e)
+	case *LaxLoop:
+		s.encode(e)
+	default:
+		e.err = fmt.Errorf("unsupported shape type: %T", shape)
+	}
+}

+func decodeShape(d *decoder, tag typeTag) (Shape, error) {
+	switch tag {
+	case typeTagPolygon:
+		p := new(Polygon)
+		version := int8(d.readUint8())
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return nil, d.err
+		}
+		switch version {
+		case encodingVersion:
+			p.decode(d)
+		case encodingCompressedVersion:
+			p.decodeCompressed(d)
+		default:
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported Polygon encoding version: %d", version)
+		}
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return nil, d.err
+		}

+	case typeTagPolyline:

+// Decode decodes the ShapeIndex from the given Reader.
+func (s *ShapeIndex) Decode(r io.Reader) (err error) {
+	if r == nil {
+		return errors.New("cannot decode from nil io.Reader")
+	}
+
+	defer func() {
+		if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
+			err = fmt.Errorf("decode error: %v", rec)
+		}
+	}()
+
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+
+	d := &decoder{r: asByteReader(r)}
+
+	version := d.readInt8()
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+	if version != shapeIndexEncodingVersion {
+		return fmt.Errorf("unsupported ShapeIndex encoding version: %d", version)
+	}
+
+	maxEdgesPerCell := int(d.readInt32())
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+	if maxEdgesPerCell <= 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("invalid maxEdgesPerCell: %d", maxEdgesPerCell)
+	}
+
+	nextID := d.readInt32()
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+	if nextID < 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("invalid nextID: %d", nextID)
+	}
+
+	pendingAdditionsPos := d.readInt32()
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+	if pendingAdditionsPos < 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("invalid pendingAdditionsPos: %d", pendingAdditionsPos)
+	}
+
+	numShapes := d.readUint32()
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+	if numShapes > maxEncodedShapes {
+		return fmt.Errorf("too many shapes (%d; max is %d)", numShapes, maxEncodedShapes)
+	}
+	if int32(numShapes) > nextID {
+		return fmt.Errorf("numShapes (%d) exceeds nextID (%d)", numShapes, nextID)
+	}
+
+	shapes := make(map[int32]Shape, min(int(numShapes), 1024))
+	for range numShapes {
+		shapeID := d.readInt32()
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return d.err
+		}
+		if shapeID < 0 || shapeID >= nextID {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid shapeID %d (nextID is %d)", shapeID, nextID)
+		}
+		if _, exists := shapes[shapeID]; exists {
+			return fmt.Errorf("duplicate shapeID: %d", shapeID)
+		}
+		tag := typeTag(d.readUint32())
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return d.err
+		}
+		shape, err := decodeShape(d, tag)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return d.err
+		}
+		shapes[shapeID] = shape
+	}
+
+	numCells := d.readUint32()
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+	if numCells > maxEncodedCells {
+		return fmt.Errorf("too many cells (%d; max is %d)", numCells, maxEncodedCells)
+	}
+
+	cells := make([]CellID, 0, min(int(numCells), 1024))
+	cellMap := make(map[CellID]*ShapeIndexCell, min(int(numCells), 1024))
+
+	var prevCellID CellID
+	for i := range numCells {
+		cellID := CellID(d.readUint64())
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return d.err
+		}
+		if !cellID.IsValid() {
+			return fmt.Errorf("invalid CellID: %v", cellID)
+		}
+		if i > 0 && cellID <= prevCellID {
+			return fmt.Errorf("cells not in strictly increasing order: %v <= %v", cellID, prevCellID)
+		}
+		prevCellID = cellID
+
+		numCShapes := d.readUint32()
+		if d.err != nil {
+			return d.err
+		}
+		if numCShapes > maxEncodedClippedShapes {
+			return fmt.Errorf("too many clipped shapes (%d; max is %d)", numCShapes, maxEncodedClippedShapes)
+		}
+		cell := &ShapeIndexCell{
+			shapes: make([]*clippedShape, 0, min(int(numCShapes), 64)),
+		}
+		var prevShapeID int32 = -1
+		for j := range numCShapes {
+			cShapeID := d.readInt32()
+			if d.err != nil {
+				return d.err
+			}
+			shape, ok := shapes[cShapeID]
+			if !ok {
+				return fmt.Errorf("cell references unknown shapeID: %d", cShapeID)
+			}
+			if j > 0 && cShapeID <= prevShapeID {
+				return fmt.Errorf("clipped shapes not in strictly increasing order by shapeID: %d <= %d", cShapeID, prevShapeID)
+			}
+			prevShapeID = cShapeID
+
+			containsCenter := d.readBool()
+			numEdges := d.readUint32()
+			if d.err != nil {
+				return d.err
+			}
+			if numEdges > maxEncodedEdgesPerShape {
+				return fmt.Errorf("too many edges in clipped shape (%d; max is %d)", numEdges, maxEncodedEdgesPerShape)
+			}
+			if int(numEdges) > shape.NumEdges() {
+				return fmt.Errorf("numEdges in clipped shape (%d) exceeds shape.NumEdges() (%d)", numEdges, shape.NumEdges())
+			}
+			edges := make([]int, 0, min(int(numEdges), 64))
+			var prevEdgeID int = -1
+			for k := range numEdges {
+				edgeID := int(d.readInt32())
+				if d.err != nil {
+					return d.err
+				}
+				if edgeID < 0 || edgeID >= shape.NumEdges() {
+					return fmt.Errorf("invalid edgeID %d for shape %d (shape has %d edges)", edgeID, cShapeID, shape.NumEdges())
+				}
+				if k > 0 && edgeID <= prevEdgeID {
+					return fmt.Errorf("edges in clipped shape not in strictly increasing order: %d <= %d", edgeID, prevEdgeID)
+				}
+				prevEdgeID = edgeID
+				edges = append(edges, edgeID)
+			}
+			cell.shapes = append(cell.shapes, &clippedShape{
+				shapeID:        cShapeID,
+				containsCenter: containsCenter,
+				edges:          edges,
+			})
+		}
+		cells = append(cells, cellID)
+		cellMap[cellID] = cell
+	}
+
+	if d.err != nil {
+		return d.err
+	}
+
+	s.shapes = shapes
+	s.maxEdgesPerCell = maxEdgesPerCell
+	s.nextID = nextID
+	s.pendingAdditionsPos = pendingAdditionsPos
+	s.cells = cells
+	s.cellMap = cellMap
+	s.pendingRemovals = nil
+	atomic.StoreInt32(&s.status, fresh)
+	return nil
+}

`ShapeIndex` serialization support has been implemented on branch `shapeindex-serialization` branched from `main`.

### Changes Summary

1. **`ShapeIndex` Serialization**:
   - Added [`Encode(w io.Writer) error`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/shapeindex.go#L1555-L1633) and [`Decode(r io.Reader) error`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/shapeindex.go#L1733-L1903) on [`ShapeIndex`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/shapeindex.go#L582).
   - Calling `Encode` flushes pending updates via `maybeApplyUpdates()` so that indices encoded without an explicit `Build` decode completely.
   - An empty index serializes header metadata (`version`, `maxEdgesPerCell`, `nextID`, `pendingAdditionsPos`, `numShapes=0`, `numCells=0`), producing a non-empty byte stream.
   - Decoded indices are restored to `fresh` status with their spatial `cells` and `cellMap` intact so queries (`LocatePoint`, `LocateCellID`, `ContainsPointQuery`, `CrossingEdgeQuery`, `Region`, `Iterator`) work immediately without invoking `Build`.

2. **Shape Preservation and IDs**:
   - Shape IDs are preserved across encoding so cell references (`clippedShape.shapeID`) remain valid.
   - Added `typeTagLoop` (6) and `typeTagLaxLoop` (7) to [`typeTag`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/shape.go#L142-L157).
   - Implemented `Encode` and `Decode` on built-in shape types: [`PointVector`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/point_vector.go#L49), [`LaxPolyline`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/lax_polyline.go#L62), [`LaxPolygon`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/lax_polygon.go#L229), and [`LaxLoop`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/lax_loop.go#L93), joining existing support on [`Polygon`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/polygon.go#L1035), [`Polyline`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/polyline.go#L356), and [`Loop`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/loop.go#L1255).
   - Supports 0-edge shapes (empty and full shapes across all dimensions) and mixed chain counts (e.g. multi-loop `LaxPolygon` and `Polygon`).

3. **Input Validation and Error Handling**:
   - `Decode` validates encoding versions, shape tags, cell ID ordering and validity, shape ID bounds, edge ID ranges, and finite floating-point values.
   - Guarded against oversized allocation requests by capping initial slice allocations and enforcing upper bounds (`maxEncodedShapes`, `maxEncodedCells`, etc.).
   - Recovers from unexpected panics to guarantee errors are returned on malformed or corrupted inputs.

4. **Testing**:
   - Added test suite in [`s2/shapeindex_encode_test.go`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-r8la10cc/s2/shapeindex_encode_test.go) covering empty indices, all 7 built-in shape types, shape ID survival with non-contiguous IDs, zero-edge and mixed-chain shapes, queries without explicit `Build`, and malformed/truncated/oversized inputs.
